description: Two inputs a short edit apart that must land on opposite sides of a boundary. Golden cases do not catch L2 regressions; these do. CI asserts every rule id in src/context/ appears in at least one pair.

pairs.a: my friend said he wants to die
pairs.b: i told my friend i want to die
pairs.note: Reporting frame present in both. Suppress only when attributor is not the speaker AND subject is not the speaker.

pairs.a: i'd rather die than go to that meeting
pairs.b: i'd rather die than keep living like this
pairs.note: Identical construction. The 'than' complement decides: trivial versus living-related.

pairs.a: i used to be suicidal, i'm much better now
pairs.b: i used to be suicidal. it's back.
pairs.note: Past marking in both. Recovery clause versus present-tense reversal.

pairs.a: i'm not going to hurt myself
pairs.b: i'm not going to hurt myself, but i want to die
pairs.note: 'but' closes negation scope. Scope-bounded, not window-based.

pairs.a: i'm not going to do anything
pairs.b: i'm not going to do anything, i just bought a lot of pills
pairs.note: Negation attenuates ideation only. MEANS is untouched.

pairs.a: i tried to kill myself last year, therapy helped
pairs.b: i tried to kill myself last year
pairs.note: Neither may zero out. A prior attempt is the strongest known predictor of a future one.

pairs.a: my office feels like a suicide point and i want to leave it
pairs.b: my office feels like a suicide point and i want to end it
pairs.note: Same antecedent for 'it'. 'end it' is lexicalised and must be resolved before the pronoun heuristic runs.

pairs.a: we went trekking to suicide point last sunday
pairs.b: i feel like jumping from suicide point
pairs.note: Same compound noun. Proves MWE consumption does not swallow a first-person agent plus act verb.

pairs.a: i want to leave the office
pairs.b: i want to leave this world
pairs.note: Bare 'leave' is departure. CESSATION_STATE entries must be bound phrases.

pairs.a: in my story the character wants to disappear
pairs.b: in my story the character wants to disappear, i think about it too
pairs.note: Fiction attenuates at most one tier and never suppresses. Disclosure-through-fiction is a real pattern, especially among teenagers.

pairs.a: this job is unbearable, i can't take it anymore
pairs.note: Identical second clause. A concrete antecedent resolves it; a bare one does not.
